channel.title: International Business Times India - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from International Business Times India (ibtimes.co.in)

item.title: Rybakina clinches maiden Aus Open crown, beats Sabalenka in summit clash
item.description: The 26-year-old Kazakh took two hours and 18 minutes to prevail 6-4, 4-6, 6-4 in the championship match, striking 28 winners en route to capturing her maiden Australian Open crown and second Grand Slam title. Rybakina, who was seeking her second Grand Slam title after winning Wimbledon in 2022, hadn't dropped a set at Melbourne Park until Saturday.

item.title: Aus Open: Japan's Tokito Oda becomes youngest man to hold all four Major titles simultaneously
item.description: At only 19 years old, Oda's victory over the third seed at Melbourne Park makes him the second man ever to win four consecutive men's wheelchair singles majors, joining Japanese legend Shingo Kunieda, who astonishingly won 12 in a row starting from 2007.

item.title: Pregnant Sonam Kapoor flaunts baby bump; trolled for 'fake' accent, fans say she looks ill as make-up couldn't hide dark circles
item.description: Sonam Kapoor opted for an off-shoulder black velvet dress as she embraced her second pregnancy. As she made her way into the event, she appeared to struggle slightly while walking and was seen holding her friend's hand for support. Her friend assisted her while they chatted, and Sonam also paused to smile for the cameras as she walked towards the event venue.

item.title: Salman Khan seeks Rs 9 crore damages; Mumbai court restrains Abhinav Kashyap from making defamatory comments
item.description: Mumbai court granted interim relief to Salman Khan, restraining filmmaker Abhinav Kashyap and others from posting, publishing or circulating any allegedly defamatory statements against him until all defendants appear in court and file their replies. The court said that free speech does not permit abusive or defamatory language.

item.title: Gold, silver prices dip 7 to 9 pc as aggressive profit taking continues
item.description: MCX gold February futures fell 7.12 per cent to Rs 1,39,000 per 10 grams around 10 am on an intraday basis. Meanwhile, MCX silver March futures dipped 9 per cent to Rs 2,65,652 per kg. CME Group raised margin requirements on Comex gold and silver futures after the metal prices saw steep declines, which raised investor caution.

item.title: Trashy ruminations by convicted criminal: MEA on PM's mention in Epstein email
item.description: India dismissed any reference to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the recently released Jeffrey Epstein files as "trashy ruminations" by a "convicted criminal." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified that aside from Modi's official visit to Israel in July 2017, the rest of the allusions in an email were baseless and should be rejected with contempt.

item.title: Cabinet clears Union Budget 2026-27; BJP hails vision for Viksit Bharat, Congress highlights need for grassroots focus
item.description: A meeting of the Union Cabinet was held at Sansad Bhawan at 10 a.m., and after the Cabinet's approval, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman proceeded to Parliament to present the Budget. Earlier, FM Sitharaman met President Droupadi Murmu and offered her a copy of the digital budget.

item.title: Trump says Iran negotiating with US
item.description: He added that "the last time they negotiated, we had to take out their nuclear. It didn't work, you know. Then we took it out a different way, and we'll see what happens." "We have a big fleet heading out there, bigger than we had -- and still have, actually -- in Venezuela," Trump said.

item.title: Sensex, Nifty open nearly flat on Budget Day
item.description: As of 9.24 am, Sensex added 9 points, or 0.01 per cent, to reach 82,278, and Nifty lost 28 points, or 0.11 per cent to settle at 25,291. Main broad-cap indices posted notable losses as the Nifty Midcap 100 declined 0.73 per cent, and the Nifty Smallcap 100 lost 1.55 per cent.

item.title: India will buy oil from Venezuela : Donald Trump's big claim
item.description: US President Donald Trumpl claimed India will buy Venezuelan oil, as opposed to purchasing oil from Iran. India does not import significant amounts of crude oil from Iran due to US sanctions, though prior to the sanctions, Iran was one of India's top sources of crude oil.
